justifications.clinical.clinicalOutcomes: Sham-controlled RCTs show no consistent benefit over standard swallowing therapy.
justifications.clinical.efficiency: 1-2 day course; moderate cost; multiple training centers available.
justifications.clinical.caseloadApplicability: Applicable to SLPs treating dysphagia; limited to this population and requires specific device.
justifications.clinical.reimbursement: Billed under electrical stimulation and dysphagia CPT codes; standard commercial and Medicare coverage at standard SLP rates.
justifications.clinical.marketDemand: Moderate employer demand in acute care and outpatient SLP dysphagia programs.
justifications.clinical.patientSatisfaction: Some patients prefer active treatment over exercises alone.
justifications.business.cashPayViability: Dysphagia treatment is overwhelmingly insurance/Medicare-funded in SNF and acute settings.
justifications.business.pricingLeverage: Branded modality with some billing leverage but no consumer premium-pricing power.
justifications.business.marketDifferentiation: Common in SLP dysphagia practice; recognizable but not rare.
justifications.business.ownerLeverage: SNF/home-health contracts can be built around dysphagia teams, but it's a commodity skill among SLPs.
justifications.business.marketDemand: Patients and families don't shop for VitalStim; referrals are clinician-driven.
justifications.business.efficiency: 1-2 day course, moderate cost; quick to obtain.
justifications.academicClinical.facultyRecognition: Commercial proprietary cert; minimal weight in SLP faculty hiring vs BCS-S.
justifications.academicClinical.scholarship: Some industry-funded studies; broader academic community is skeptical.
justifications.academicClinical.teachingValue: Useful for teaching e-stim modules within dysphagia coursework.
justifications.academicClinical.evidenceDepth: Evidence for NMES in dysphagia is mixed and contested in systematic reviews.
justifications.academicClinical.facultyDemand: Rarely listed in SLP faculty postings.
justifications.academicClinical.efficiency: Quick to earn, but low academic payoff.
